pages.raw_meta: As a leading distributor and manufacturer of building materials, at Boise Cascade®, we bring people, products, and services together to build strong homes, businesses, and communities that stand the test of time.
raw_blocks: As a leading distributor and manufacturer of building materials, at Boise Cascade ® , we bring people, products, and services together to build strong homes, businesses, and communities that stand the test of time.

Together with our associates, customers, suppliers, vendors, and communities, we've helped support the mission of St. Jude Children's Research Hospital®: Finding cures. Saving children®. Every contribution helps advance groundbreaking research and provides hope to families when they need it most.

We are honored to be named one of America's Best Large Employers in 2026 by Forbes. This recognition highlights our commitment to being a great place to work by fostering a culture of connection and community for all associates. We provide meaningful engagement, ongoing development opportunities, and a supportive environment that empowers associates to excel, grow their skills, and build lasting careers.

We're proud to have recently been named one of America’s Most Trustworthy Companies of 2026 by Newsweek. This recognition is based on an assessment across three key pillars of trust: customer trust, investor trust, and employee trust. Of the thousands of companies considered for this recognition, only 700 earned the honor. Boise Cascade ranked in the Top 12 within the Construction category.

We are one of the largest U.S. wholesale distributors of building materials and a leading manufacturer of engineered wood products and plywood in North America. Our integrated model and national distribution footprint position us to deliver outstanding service to our customers across a broad range of industry-leading products, including key structural products that we produce.

Headquartered in Boise, Idaho, we operate more than 60 distribution and manufacturing facilities strategically located across the U.S. and Canada. Our work is powered by a dedicated team of over 7,500 people. Our shared values drive our daily business decisions, and we pride ourselves on being a consistent, reliable, and trustworthy partner for our customers and suppliers.
We are a Fortune 1000 company with $6.4B in annual sales (2025). The Company is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol BCC.

We operate two divisions, supported by a corporate shared services model. Capitalizing on the synergies of both manufacturing and distribution enables us to fulfill the needs for new homes and repair/remodel in the residential and light commercial construction industry.
Distributes building products on a wholesale basis, offering everything from wood products, siding, composite decking, metal, insulation, roofing, and more
Operates 39 branches nationwide and 15 millwork door shops
Manufactures lumber, plywood, and environmentally friendly engineered wood products
Operates a network of mills in the Pacific Northwest and Southeastern regions of the U.S., and one plant in New Brunswick, Canada
The history of Boise Cascade is a story of determination, flexibility, and resilience.

From a legal perspective, our Company’s history begins in 2004 when Boise Cascade as we know it today was legally formed. While the legal origin of our current Company is important, our roots run much deeper, and the work, people, and legacy that shape our Company go back decades before 2004. The intersection between our legal origin and the full story creates a complex history. We are proud of our deep roots, and we believe our journey is an important part of what makes Boise Cascade who and what we are today.

Boise Cascade Corporation was formed in 1957 through the merger of Cascade Lumber Company of Yakima, WA, and Boise Payette Lumber Company of Boise, ID. The early days focused on growing and harvesting timber, and manufacturing and distributing lumber and building products.

Opportunity and boldness led to the exploration of other industries over the years, including paper, shipping containers, concrete, sand and gravel, real estate, and recreation, including ownership of a motor home manufacturer.

In the 1990s, Boise Cascade Corporation invested in engineered wood products (EWP) and building mills in Oregon and Louisiana for producing laminated veneer lumber (LVL). Furman Lumber of Billerica, MA, was purchased, which paved the way to a nationwide building materials wholesale distribution system.

The next decade continued to bring big changes. In 2003, Boise Cascade Corporation acquired OfficeMax and adopted OfficeMax as its own name. Shortly after that, in 2004, OfficeMax sold its non-office products businesses and the name “Boise Cascade” to a private equity firm, which started Boise Cascade Company as it exists today.
In 2008, the housing market collapsed, and the Great Recession ensued. The Company survived and began its slow recovery through strategic investments in EWP and building materials distribution.

By late 2012, the Company had successfully recovered and began preparing to launch an initial public offering (IPO). The IPO was completed on February 6, 2013, and the Company rang the bell at the New York Stock Exchange that day.
